title: Warm Climates May Have Helped Crocodile Kin Outlast the Dinosaurs
paragraphs: Sixty-six million years ago, an asteroid hit Earth and most dinosaurs died. Crocodiles and their relatives survived. A new study from University College London tries to explain why.
The scientists looked at more than 7,000 fossils and records from over 400 species. They learned which temperatures and rain each species liked. Then they used computer models of old climates.

The models suggest that crocodile relatives mostly lived in warm places. After the asteroid, the area near the equator stayed warm enough for them. Dinosaurs lost much more of their homes. The scientists say that warmth was probably not the only reason.

questions.q: What did the scientists use besides fossils?
What did the area near the equator offer?
questions.a: It stayed warm enough for crocodile relatives.
